subject: Not dearer milk, but 'W20 Milk': 20 per cent water, free
alt: Viju's cartoon: on the right a moustachioed milkman in a green kurta and a blue headband stands pouring milk from a steel measure into a vessel. On the left a woman in an orange-red sari stands at a door, eyes wide, looking on in alarm. The milkman's speech bubble says in Hindi: I did not raise the price. Instead I have launched W20 Milk. It will have 20% water added. At the upper left is the BBC News Hindi logo, and at the right a box reads: Amul and Mother Dairy have raised milk prices. The cartoonist's signature is at the lower left.
chutki: Amul and Mother Dairy raised milk prices from 12 November. In the cartoon the milkman does not deny the rise; he gives it a new name: 'W20 Milk', with twenty per cent water added. So the price went up and the milk went down.

Viju's joke turns on 'W20', the name of the women's track within the G20. In the language of summits 'W20' sounds grand and official, but the milk is the same, only its share of water has grown. Calling inflation a 'new product launch' is the real joke.
